identification.summary: Proofpoint tracks TA829 as a cybercriminal actor that occasionally also conducts espionage aligned with Russian state interests; Proofpoint dates the espionage activity to after the invasion of Ukraine, alongside ongoing financially motivated campaigns [S1][S2]. Its toolset is built around variants of the RomCom backdoor, including SingleCamper (espionage-focused) and DustyHammock (financially motivated), delivered by a loader family Proofpoint calls SlipScreen [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Proofpoint separately tracks UNK_GreenSec, a cluster using TransferLoader that shares infrastructure and delivery tactics with TA829; Proofpoint currently treats it as a separate cybercriminal cluster and says it is unclear whether the two collaborate or are one entity [S1][S2]. RomCom as a malware family and group name is also used by ESET and others; ESET described a Russia-aligned RomCom APT group exploiting Firefox and Windows zero-days in late 2024 [S3][S4]. Trend Micro tracks Void Rabisu (also reported as Storm-0978, Tropical Scorpius, UNC2596) tied to RomCom RAT [S6]. Whether these vendor clusters equal TA829 is not established in the sources opened, so they are not merged here. Pages were read through search-result summaries only; direct fetches failed.

attribution.sponsor: No government attribution found. Proofpoint describes the espionage activity as aligned with Russian state interests, while describing the actor as primarily cybercriminal [S1][S2].
attribution.confidence: Proofpoint frames TA829 as a hybrid cybercriminal and espionage actor and states it is unclear if TA829 and UNK_GreenSec are the same entity [S1][S2]. ESET labels the RomCom group Russia-aligned [S3]. Trend Micro, for Void Rabisu, reported no evidence of state sponsorship and suggested a criminal actor drawn into espionage by the war in Ukraine [S6].
attribution.basis: Vendor reporting on malware overlap (RomCom variants, SlipScreen loader) and shared infrastructure [S1][S2]. Primary Proofpoint text was not opened; details come from search summaries of it and secondary coverage.

objectives: Mixed motives per Proofpoint: financially motivated cybercrime plus occasional espionage aligned with Russian state interests [S1][S2].

targeting.notes: Lures reported by secondary coverage of Proofpoint use job-application and security-breach themes sent from freemail accounts [S1][S2]. Sector and regional victim lists for TA829 were not verified. For the RomCom group generally, ESET reported victims of the Firefox/Windows zero-day chain were located mostly in Europe and North America [S4]; coverage of the 2023 RomCom RAT reports focus on Ukraine and countries supporting it, and female political leaders attending a June 2023 summit [S6]. Those are RomCom-family findings, not confirmed TA829 findings.

capabilities.summary: Phishing from freemail accounts with job-application or security-breach lures leading to spoofed OneDrive or Google Drive pages [S1][S2]. SlipScreen loader leads to downloaders MeltingClaw/RustyClaw, then ShadyHammock or DustyHammock backdoors; ShadyHammock launches SingleCamper (updated RomCom RAT, also tracked as SnipBot); DustyHammock can fetch payloads from IPFS [S1][S2]. Infrastructure uses REM Proxy nodes on compromised MikroTik routers, likely rented out to relay traffic; the routers commonly have port 51922 open running SSH, and how they were compromised is unknown [S1][S2]. The wider RomCom group exploited Firefox CVE-2024-9680 and Windows Task Scheduler CVE-2024-49039 as zero-days in late 2024 per ESET, and Word CVE-2023-36884 in 2023 [S3][S4][S5].

campaigns.name: RomCom family: CVE-2023-36884 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Reporting describes the RomCom group's first known in-the-wild zero-day, a Microsoft Word flaw, in June 2023. Link to TA829 specifically is unconfirmed.

campaigns.name: RomCom family: PEAPOD / fake Women Political Leaders Summit site
campaigns.summary: Reported October 2023 (Trend Micro via The Hacker News): a slimmed-down RomCom variant was delivered via a fake summit site and targeted female political leaders who attended the June 2023 summit. Link to TA829 specifically is unconfirmed.

campaigns.name: RomCom family: Firefox and Windows zero-day chain
campaigns.summary: ESET found Firefox CVE-2024-9680 on 8 October 2024, patched by Mozilla the next day; chained with Windows CVE-2024-49039, patched 12 November, to install a RomCom backdoor with no user interaction beyond visiting a page. Victims were mostly in Europe and North America. Google TAG independently found the Windows flaw.

campaigns.name: Proofpoint publication on TA829 and UNK_GreenSec
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reported TA829 and UNK_GreenSec share REM Proxy nodes on MikroTik routers, delivery tactics and loader behavior, with TA829 using SlipScreen and SingleCamper/DustyHammock and UNK_GreenSec using TransferLoader.

diamond.adversary: Hybrid cybercriminal and espionage actor with Russia-aligned espionage activity; relationship to UNK_GreenSec unresolved [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: RomCom variants (SingleCamper, DustyHammock), SlipScreen loader, MeltingClaw/RustyClaw downloaders, ShadyHammock [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: REM Proxy nodes on compromised MikroTik routers; spoofed OneDrive and Google Drive pages; IPFS payload hosting [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Not verified for TA829. Phishing recipients receive job-application or security-breach lures [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage aligned with Russian state interests alongside profit-driven operations, per Proofpoint [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints reached via phishing; internet-exposed MikroTik routers abused as relays; for the wider RomCom group, unpatched browsers (Firefox) and Windows [S1][S2][S3].

gaps: Proofpoint's primary blog (10 Things I Hate About Attribution: RomCom vs. TransferLoader) and ESET's blog could not be fetched; facts come from search-result summaries and secondary coverage and should be checked against the originals.
First-observed date for TA829 is not established in the sources gathered.
Victim sectors, regions and campaign dates specific to TA829 are not verified.

Relationship between TA829, UNK_GreenSec, ESET's RomCom group and Trend Micro's Void Rabisu (Storm-0978) is unresolved; no source opened states they are the same cluster. Trend Micro reported no evidence of state sponsorship for Void Rabisu [S6].
How MikroTik routers were compromised is unknown [S1][S2].
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID or Microsoft name was confirmed for TA829.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain includes email and web-mail users, endpoints that can reach Google Drive and OneDrive, and internet-facing routers that may be conscripted as proxies. STEP 2: The actor mixes criminal and espionage tasking, so defenders may see ransomware-style or fraud activity from the same toolset. STEP 3: Template is freemail phishing with job or breach lures, spoofed cloud-storage page, SlipScreen, downloader, backdoor, RomCom RAT; wider RomCom group has used browser and Windows zero-days. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued phishing against organizations with a mix of criminal and espionage payoffs. MDCOA is zero-day browser exploitation (as ESET saw in 2024) against government or defense personnel. Candidate indicators: SSH on port 51922 on MikroTik devices, traffic to spoofed Drive/OneDrive pages, IPFS retrievals from endpoints [S1][S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor reporting on TA829, UNK_GreenSec and RomCom as potentially overlapping, and avoid merging cluster names. (2) Authorities: router-relay infrastructure is often civilian or foreign-owned, so blocking and takedown need coordination through appropriate cyber authorities. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize rapid browser and Windows patching and phishing-resistant mail filtering for personnel mailboxes. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partners via DC3/DIB programs and allied CERTs, given reported Europe and North America victimization [S1][S2][S4].
